### Problem: Divisor game {#sec-pf-p2-divisor}

::: {.p-statement}
Start with $n$ ($1 \le n \le 1000$). On a turn, choose $x$ with $0 < x < n$ and $x \mid n$, and replace $n$ by $n - x$. A player who cannot move loses. Alice moves first. Does Alice win with optimal play?

Source: [LC 1025 · Divisor Game](https://leetcode.com/problems/divisor-game/){.solved difficulty="Easy"}
:::

::: {.p-intuition}
The table shows Alice wins exactly for even $n$. An even player can always subtract 1 and hand over an odd number; an odd number has only odd divisors, so the opponent must hand back an even number.
:::

::: {.p-approach}
**Claim:** $n$ is winning iff $n$ is even. Strong induction on $n$.

- *Base:* $n = 1$ has no move: losing, and 1 is odd. ✓
- *$n$ even:* $x = 1$ is a legal move to $n - 1$, which is odd and so losing by hypothesis. Winning.
- *$n$ odd, $n > 1$:* every divisor $x$ of an odd number is odd, so $n - x$ is even, which is winning by hypothesis. Every move leads to a winning position: losing.
:::

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
#### Python

```{python}
#| label: pf-divisor
def divisor_game(n):
    return n % 2 == 0

@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
def divisor_brute(n):
    return any(not divisor_brute(n - x) for x in range(1, n) if n % x == 0)

assert all(divisor_brute(n) == divisor_game(n) for n in range(1, 301))
```

#### C++

```cpp
bool divisorGame(int n) { return n % 2 == 0; }
```
:::

::: {#fig-pf-divisor}

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    ns = list(range(1, 13))
    row = ["W" if divisor_brute(n) else "L" for n in ns]
    assert row == ["W" if n % 2 == 0 else "L" for n in ns]
    V.grid(ax, p, [ns, row], row_labels=["n", ""], colors={(1, i): ("green" if r == "W" else "red") for i, r in enumerate(row)})
V.show(draw)
```

Divisor game positions 1..12 from the brute force: exactly the even numbers are winning. From an even n the move x = 1 lands on an odd (losing) number.

:::

::: {.p-complexity}
**Time** $O(1)$. The brute force is $O(n\sqrt n)$ with divisor enumeration (or $O(n^2)$ as written), which is fine for $n \le 1000$ but the proof is the real answer.
:::

::: {.p-edge}
- $n = 1$: Alice cannot move and loses.
- The key lemma — odd numbers have only odd divisors — is where the proof uses the game's specific rule; check such lemmas separately.
:::
